entries.test: Meta’s public investment disclosures and strategic announcements through April 2023 would show whether it shifted priority from the metaverse to AI and identified AI as its largest investment.
entries.note: The investment wording quotes Zuckerberg, but Zitron endorses it as evidence for his own assertion of a pivot.
The AI spending component is explicitly an assumption. The cancellation and cost-saving assertion could be checked separately.

entries.test: Meta’s public metaverse commitments, investments, and product activity around its AI pivot would show whether Zuckerberg abandoned the metaverse at that time.
entries.note: “Gave up” has a plain operational reading as abandoning the initiative; the emphatic timing does not eliminate that factual commitment.

entries.test: Meta’s public strategy changes and the competitive performance of its products modeled on rivals would show whether the asserted abandonment and repeated competitive failures occurred.
entries.note: “Whatever interests Wall Street more” broadens a reference to this particular pivot into a general rule. The source nevertheless asserts an abandonment and a factual track record.
